name: Rua Negra
description:
Rua Negra began in 2207 as a three-person project operating out of a Circuit-tier rehearsal space above a noodle shop near the old Kenosha transit hub: vocalist and producer Marisol Takeda-Okonkwo, electronic composer and BCI-artist Nneka Ferreira-Johansson, and live percussionist and beatmaker Tariq Vasquez-Elmi. Their sound draws from Brazilian baile funk, Japanese noise, West African highlife, and the particular sonic texture of GLMZ's urban infrastructure — they have sampled rainfall on corrugated steel rooftops, the resonance of the elevated transit lines, the specific frequency hum of the Shelf's aging power grid. Marisol's vocals are multilingual and deliberately non-translated: Portuguese, Igbo, Japanese, and a constructed patois that has developed organically in the Circuit's most densely mixed neighborhoods.

What distinguishes Rua Negra from most Circuit acts is their deliberate cross-tier ambition — not aspiration, but provocation. Their 2215 album 'Corrente' was released simultaneously on pirate mesh (free), physical chip (Φ3 at shows), and licensed neural feed (Φ180 per stream). The pricing was a statement. The music was good enough that all three markets responded. Spire critics called it 'raw but compelling.' Shelf kids called it theirs. The Circuit, which made it, called it home.
creator: Marisol Takeda-Okonkwo, Nneka Ferreira-Johansson, Tariq Vasquez-Elmi
genre: Cross-Tier Electronic, Polyglot Funk, Urban Sampling, BCI-Integrated
audience: Circuit youth, Shelf music scenes, Tier 3 club-goers, Spire avant-garde listeners, BCI-augmented music communities
cultural_impact: Rua Negra is one of the few acts in GLMZ's recent history to achieve genuine cross-tier cultural penetration without corporate machinery behind them — and without losing credibility in the lower tiers in the process. Their simultaneous multi-tier release model has been widely discussed in music industry circles and has been imitated, poorly, by several Vantablack subsidiaries attempting to manufacture an 'authentic' underground appeal. The band's response was to release a diss track titled 'Simulation Fee' that named three subsidiary labels by name and is currently the subject of a Vantablack defamation filing.
story_hooks: Vantablack's defamation suit against Rua Negra is scheduled to go before a corporate arbitration panel — a process so stacked against independent artists that even winning is ruinous. Nneka Ferreira-Johansson is quietly looking for documentation of Vantablack's own illegal practices that might shift the leverage.

Tariq Vasquez-Elmi has been approached by a Tier 5 private collector offering an obscene sum for the original master recordings of 'Corrente' — the other two members don't know, and Tariq hasn't decided, and someone has already started following him.

A new Rua Negra track is circulating on pirate mesh that none of the three members claim to have made — it sounds exactly like them, down to Marisol's vocal patterns, and it contains coordinates embedded in the audio metadata.
